**Q8: Where does the heavy script live?**

`mise.toml` already holds short bash heredocs. The local-release script is going to be ~150 lines (preflight, version detection, two docker buildx invocations, goreleaser, gh release upload). Inline gets unreadable fast.

| Option | Path | Tradeoff |
|---|---|---|
| **A. `scripts/release.sh`** | New top-level `scripts/` dir | Conventional, no naming surprise. New dir, but mise.toml already references `installer/build.sh` so precedent exists. |
| **B. `bin/release`** | Rails-style `bin/` | Matches Rails convention (`bin/dev`, `bin/ci`). But `bin/` is for runtime tools, not build/dev tooling — putting a release script there is a category mismatch. |
| **C. `installer/release.sh`** | Reuse the installer dir | Bad — installer is for end-user installs. Conflates two concerns. |
| **D. `vendor/sandcastle-cli/Makefile` extension** | Extend the existing CLI Makefile (which already has `make build`) | Half the script (CLI build) lives there naturally. But the script also builds Docker images and uploads installer.sh — neither belongs in the CLI's Makefile. Splits the script across two locations. |

Recommendation: **A** — `scripts/release.sh`. Single file, one purpose, easy to find.
